---
title: NetCDF
---
On the output side, the NetCDF format for data storage is used in two ways:
*   Save and load model state
*   Write output on a time step basis

The central function facilitating NetCDF output is
    `write_netcdf_timestep` in `io.jl`

For more information on the NetCDF standard we refer to the official documentation at [UniData](https://www.unidata.ucar.edu/software/netcdf)

More details on the application of this file format within Wflow can be found in the [HydroMT-Wflow](https://deltares.github.io/hydromt_wflow/stable/index.html). More specific, the use of NetCDF is  described in the sections:

* [Model methods](https://deltares.github.io/hydromt_wflow/model_methods/)
 in relation to input and output for the Wflow model itself

* [Data Catalog preparation](https://deltares.github.io/hydromt_wflow/data_catalog/) → specifying NetCDF sources

* [Model building workflow](https://deltares.github.io/hydromt_wflow/model_building/) → conversion to CF‑compliant NetCDF

<hr>

## NetCDF for time-varying or fixed atmospheric forcing
* initially set fixed atmospheric forcing
 `load_fixed_forcing` → `get_field_in_model`
* update atmospheric forcing for a given time
 `update_forcing` → `get_at`

 The list of names of the atmospheric quantities is enclosed in the `reader` which is part of the `model`.
 This list of names is part of the model configuration.

## NetCDF for static model layers

The model opens `input.path_static` during initialization. Model components read their
parameters from this dataset with `ncread` in [`utils.jl`](../../Wflow/src/utils.jl), then
the dataset is closed after model construction. The `[input.static]` table maps Wflow
standard names to NetCDF variable names; for example, `river__length = "wflow_riverlength"`.
An input can instead be specified as a uniform TOML value. If an optional parameter is not
mapped, its metadata default is used when one is defined.

For NetCDF-backed values, `ncread` reads the first time slice (if a `time` dimension is
present), standardizes the spatial axes, applies configured scale and offset, and selects
the requested active cells. It handles missing and NaN values according to the parameter
metadata, then converts the data to the expected type and SI units. Layered parameters also
read their layer dimension and can apply layer-specific scale and offset values.

## NetCDF for atmospheric forcing

The `[input.forcing]` table maps Wflow standard names to variables in `input.path_forcing`,
for example precipitation, potential evaporation, and air temperature. These mappings are
stored in the model's `NCReader`, which sorts forcing files by their time values and keeps
the currently needed file open. A glob can be used when forcing is split across files.

At each timestep, `update_forcing!` in [`io.jl`](../../Wflow/src/io.jl) selects the first
forcing timestamp at or after the model time. Wflow expects right-labelled forcing: a
timestamp marks the end of its accumulation interval. The read field is scaled and offset,
converted to the parameter's expected type and SI units, and reduced to the active model
cells. Missing values on active cells are rejected. Precipitation and potential evaporation
are averaged over reservoir coverage and passed to reservoir boundary fields when reservoirs
are enabled.

Forcing entries may also be constant values in the TOML configuration. These are loaded
once by `load_fixed_forcing!`; NetCDF-backed forcing values are refreshed each timestep.

## Cyclic parameters

Cyclic parameters are also read from `input.path_static`, but are configured separately in
`[input.cyclic]`. Their NetCDF variable must have a time dimension whose name starts with
`time`. Wflow reads the cyclic data during initialization and updates the corresponding
model fields on the configured cycle, rather than treating them as static parameters or
ordinary timestep forcing.
